name: Mate with king and queen
goal: You can mate a lone king with king and queen, pushing it to the edge without giving stalemate.
intro: With a king and a queen against a lone king you can always force mate, and with the best moves it never takes more than ten. First the queen works on its own: it shuts the enemy king into a smaller and smaller box until the king reaches the edge of the board. Then your own king walks over to help, because a queen cannot give mate without it. Take care at the end: if the lone king has no legal move and is not in check, the game is a draw by stalemate.

parts.title: Shrink the box
parts.keyIdea: The queen alone can fence the king into a box; keep it a knight's jump from the king and the box only gets smaller.
parts.text: A worked example from Wikibooks. Your king is far away in the corner, so for now the queen works alone. Black's king stands in the middle: find a queen move that fences it in, without giving check.
parts.line: Qb5 Ke6 Qc5 Kf6 Qd5 Kg6 Qe5

notes.text: The queen takes the whole fifth rank and the b-file, so Black's king cannot come down to the fifth rank or cross to the b-file. It stands a knight's jump from the king (two files across, one rank down), close enough to take squares away but out of the king's reach.

The king stepped to e6, so the queen follows to c5, again a knight's jump away. Now the c-file is shut too. A check is not needed: Qc6+ would leave the fifth rank, and the king could walk back down through e5 or f5.
Same pattern: the king went to f6, the queen goes to d5. Black's king can no longer use the d-file or the fifth rank, so its box keeps getting smaller.
The king keeps running to the side, and the queen keeps following it. After Qe5 Black's king is shut into the f-, g- and h-files, above the fifth rank.

parts.title: Pin the king to the edge
parts.keyIdea: Once the lone king is stuck on the edge, stop chasing it and bring your own king over to help.
parts.text: The same example, one move later, with Black to move. Keep shrinking the box with the queen until Black's king is stuck on the edge of the board, then think about your king on a1.
parts.line: Kf7 Qd6 Kg7 Qe6 Kh7 Qg4 Kh6 Kb2

notes.text: The king went to f7, so the queen goes to d6, a knight's jump away once more. It shuts the sixth rank, and from d6 it also covers e7 and f8, so Black's king is left with the top two ranks.
The same step again. The queen on e6 covers the sixth rank, the e-file, f7 and g8, so the king is squeezed towards the corner.

Black's king has reached the edge. With the queen on g4 the whole g-file is shut, so the king can only walk up and down the h-file, between h6 and h8. It still has a square to go to, so there is no stalemate.
Black's king cannot get off the h-file, so the queen's job is done for now. Your king leaves the corner and walks over to help: the queen cannot give mate on its own.

parts.title: Mate, and beware of stalemate
parts.keyIdea: Mate needs your king's help; before every move, check that the lone king still has a legal move.
parts.text: The same example a few moves later: your king has arrived on e5, and Black's king is in the corner on h8. Bring your king close enough to protect the queen. Careful: Qg6 here looks strong, but it would leave Black with no legal move and no check, which is stalemate.

notes.text: Your king steps next to g7, the square where the queen wants to give mate. Black's king still has h7 to go to, so this is not stalemate.
Mate. The queen checks from g7 and Black's king cannot take it, because your king on f6 guards it. The queen also covers g8, h8, g6 and h6, so the king has nowhere to go.
